paper_title: Memorization and Knowledge Injection in Gated LLMs
caption: Analysis on the embedding quality in Llama intermediate layers. Correct gate rate is computed as the rate of question embeddings which have the maximum inner product with the relevant passage embedding. It is computed for each dataset partition, which has 50 passage samples. Shaded area is the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions. We found that embeddings at the input of MLP layers are better than at the input of attention layers. We choose to use last MLP layer input as embedding in the main experiments of MEGa.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the average correct gate rate across different embedding layer inputs for several models. The x-axis represents the embedding layer, ranging from 0 to 30, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 5, and utilizes a linear scale. The y-axis represents the average correct gate rate, ranging from approximately 0.35 to 0.85 with tick labels spaced at intervals of 0.05, and also employs a linear scale. A solid blue line represents the average correct gate rate for the Character Attention input, beginning at approximately 0.61 and decreasing to approximately 0.43. A dashed blue line represents the correct gate rate for the Wiki Attention input, beginning at approximately 0.52 and decreasing to approximately 0.30. Finally, a solid red line represents the average correct gate rate for the Wiki MLP input, beginning at approximately 0.63 and decreasing to approximately 0.40 and a dashed red line represents the correct gate rate for the Wiki MLP input, beginning at approximately 0.61 and decreasing to approximately 0.41. A light purple shaded region surrounds the blue line, indicating the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions, with a maximum value of approximately 0.06 at x = 10 and a minimum value of approximately 0.02 at x = 0.
